title: Roots on vs off: the same grove at 24,000 frames
question: Which of these reads as a wood standing in ground? Same world, same seed, same frame, one constant apart.
context_md:
Counts for THESE two runs, not a lab bed: standing cells 21,932 -> 28,390; ROOT cells 1,662 -> 6,545 (3.94x); shoot 20,270 -> 21,845; root:shoot 8.2% -> 30.0%; live plants 197 -> 335.

The change: a root tip used to stop growing as soon as the plant read itself as watered, and it nearly always did, because that reading was taken against a water store that grows with the root count. It now asks about the soil it is actually standing in. Second constant, which had to move with it: the store stops growing without limit with root count, so a plant dying of thirst can no longer root its way to a bigger bucket and read as well-watered.

What I am NOT sure of and would like your eye on: the off arm's ground appears to have drained out from under the grove, leaving trees on rafts. If that is what the game has looked like all along, it is a bigger finding than the roots. Both arms are one binary, scene=grove start=24000, daylight pinned; the off arm is PIXEL_PHYSICS_ROOT_GATE=whole with an unbounded tank.
